questions.text: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell' and produces most of the cell's ATP?

options.option_text: Nucleus — stores genetic information as DNA
Ribosome — assembles proteins from amino acids
Mitochondrion — carries out cellular respiration
Lysosome — digests worn-out cellular components

questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration (oxidative phosphorylation), generating the bulk of a cell's ATP via the electron transport chain. They have their own circular DNA, double membrane (outer + inner with cristae), and are thought to have evolved from symbiotic bacteria (endosymbiont theory).

options.option_text: producing energy via the citric acid cycle
synthesising proteins by translating mRNA sequences
digesting pathogens using hydrolytic enzymes
packaging proteins into vesicles for secretion

questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA sequences and assemble amino acids into polypeptide chains — the process of translation. They can be free in the cytoplasm (making cytoplasmic proteins) or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (making secretory/membrane proteins). They are not membrane-bound organelles.

questions.text: Which organelle–function pairing is CORRECTLY matched?

options.option_text: Golgi apparatus — primary site of ATP production
Lysosome — performs photosynthesis using chlorophyll
Vacuole — stores water, sap, and metabolic waste
Chloroplast — digests foreign particles by hydrolysis

questions.explanation: Vacuoles (especially the large central vacuole in plant cells) store water, cell sap, pigments, and metabolic waste; they also maintain turgor pressure. Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins/lipids; Lysosome performs intracellular digestion; Chloroplast carries out photosynthesis.

questions.text: During mitosis, chromosomes align at the cell's equatorial plate during which phase?

options.option_text: Prophase — chromosomes condense and become visible
Metaphase — chromosomes line up at the cell equator
Anaphase — sister chromatids separate toward poles
Telophase — nuclear envelopes reform around chromosomes

questions.explanation: In metaphase, maximally condensed chromosomes align along the metaphase plate (cell equator), attached to spindle fibres at their centromeres. This ensures equal distribution to daughter cells. Metaphase provides the clearest view of chromosome number and morphology, making it ideal for karyotyping.

questions.text: The cell membrane is called 'selectively permeable' because ____.

options.option_text: it lets all molecules pass freely without any restriction
it permits only pure water molecules to cross at all times
it controls which substances can enter or exit the cell
it blocks all ionic and large molecular movement completely

questions.explanation: Selective permeability means the membrane allows small nonpolar molecules and water to pass freely, while regulating ions and polar/large molecules through protein channels, carriers, and pumps. This selective control maintains the cell's internal environment (homeostasis). Neither completely open nor completely closed.

questions.text: A plant cell is placed in a hypertonic solution. Which sequence correctly describes the outcome?

options.option_text: Water enters → vacuole enlarges → turgor builds → cell bursts (lysis)
Water exits → cytoplasm shrinks → membrane pulls from wall → plasmolysis
Water enters → membrane ruptures → cell wall collapses inward
Water exits → vacuole fills with solutes → osmotic pressure equalises quickly

questions.explanation: In a hypertonic solution (higher solute outside), water exits the cell by osmosis. The vacuole shrinks, the cytoplasm contracts, and the plasma membrane pulls away from the rigid cell wall — this is plasmolysis. Cell lysis (bursting) occurs in hypotonic solutions when water enters. The plant cell wall prevents physical bursting.

questions.text: Which statement about the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Rough ER bears ribosomes and is involved in protein synthesis
Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and handles lipid synthesis and detoxification
Both rough and smooth ER are physically connected to the nuclear envelope
Rough ER is the primary site for ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation

questions.explanation: ATP synthesis via oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE (via ATP synthase), not the rough ER. The rough ER handles co-translational protein synthesis and folding. All other options are correct: rough ER has ribosomes, smooth ER handles lipids/detox, and both are continuous with the nuclear envelope.
